lines.english: ...The bathroom...

lines.japanese: ……アレキサンダーの、便所か。
lines.english: ...Alexander's bathroom.

lines.japanese: ……よし。
lines.english: ...Right.

lines.japanese: よし。
lines.english: All right.

lines.japanese: 俺はゆっくり首を回し、膝に力を入れて便座から立ちあがった。
lines.english: I slowly rolled my neck, braced my knees, and rose from the toilet seat.

lines.japanese: かさ。
lines.english: Rustle.

lines.japanese: その拍子に、手から何かがこぼれた。目で追うと、足元の床に紙くずが転がっている。どうやら俺は、それを右のこぶしに握っていたみたいだ。
lines.english: Something slipped from my hand as I stood. I followed it with my eyes and found a crumpled scrap of paper on the floor at my feet. Apparently I'd been clutching it in my right fist.

lines.japanese: 拾いあげて皺を伸ばしてみる。
lines.english: I picked it up and smoothed out the creases.

lines.japanese: 『今日からアレキサンダーでバイトを始めました』
lines.english: “I started working at Alexander today.”

lines.japanese: 大人ぶった柔らかい筆跡。鷲介の字だ。
lines.english: Soft handwriting with a grown-up affectation. Shusuke's.

lines.japanese: 『ちょっぴり遅くなっちゃったけど、初日だから大目に見てね。怒っちゃいやよ。世界が平和でありますように──』
lines.english: “I may be just a teensy bit late, but it's my first day, so please let it slide. Don't be mad, okay? *May peace prevail on Earth*—”

lines.japanese: ──ハァト。
lines.english: —Heart.

lines.japanese: 「ハートじゃねえだろタコ。こっちのハートは震えねンだよ」
lines.english: “Heart, my ass, you idiot. Mine isn’t trembling one damn bit.”

lines.japanese: 俺は広げた紙くずを丸めた紙くずに戻して、くず箱の底に叩きつけた。
lines.english: I crushed the unfolded scrap back into a ball and slammed it into the bottom of the trash can.

lines.japanese: 怒ってねえよ、呆れてるんだ。そもそも、いまぐだぐだと文句を並べたてたところで≪待機室≫に篭ったあいつの耳にはもう届かない。
lines.english: I wasn't angry. I was appalled. Besides, no matter how long I stood there listing my grievances, they would never reach the brat now shut away in the *Waiting Room*.

lines.japanese: 「クソガキが、近いうち≪面談≫の必要ありだな……」
lines.english: “Damn brat. We’re going to need an *Interview* soon...”

lines.japanese: アレはアレで疲れるから嫌なんだけど。
lines.english: Not that I wanted one. Those things were exhausting in their own way.

lines.japanese: 「めんどくせえ。ブッ殺すぞアノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What a fucking nuisance. I'll kill that bastard.”

lines.japanese: 俺はすぐそばの台に置かれていたスポーツバッグを開けて、自分の服を引っぱりだす。
lines.english: I opened the sports bag on the nearby counter and pulled out my own clothes.

lines.japanese: こんなチャラい服、着てられるか。
lines.english: Like hell I was going to wear this tacky getup.

lines.japanese: 便所から出て店の壁時計を見た。１０時５５分。
lines.english: I left the bathroom and checked the clock on the restaurant wall. 10:55.

lines.japanese: あのヤロウ、何がちょっぴりだ。約束の時間を二十五分も過ぎてるじゃねえか。
lines.english: Teensy bit, my ass. The bastard was twenty-five minutes past the time we'd agreed on.

lines.japanese: 「どうした鷲介、着替えたのか」
lines.english: “What happened, Shusuke? You changed clothes?”

lines.japanese: さっさと帰ろうとしたら、厨房から不精髭のおっさんが出てきた。たしか……他の従業員に店長と呼ばれているのを何度か耳にしたことがあった。
lines.english: I was about to make a quick exit when some stubbled old guy emerged from the kitchen. I was fairly sure I'd heard the other employees call him the manager a few times.

lines.japanese: もちろん俺は返事などせず、何も聞こえなかったふりをしてすたすた出口へ向かった。それぞれの知人とは極力接触を避けるのが、俺たちの数多い≪取り決め≫のひとつだ。
lines.english: Naturally, I didn't answer. I pretended not to hear and strode toward the exit. Avoiding one another's acquaintances as far as possible was one of the many terms in our *Agreement*.

lines.japanese: 「おい鷲介、ちょっと待ってくれ」
lines.english: “Hey, Shusuke. Wait a moment.”

lines.japanese: しかし、この場合の「極力」とは「相手に不信感を抱かせない範囲内で」という意味でもある。雇用主の制止を無視するのは、おそらく鷲介にとって問題行動なんだろう。
lines.english: But here, ‘as far as possible’ also meant ‘so long as it didn't make the other person suspicious.’ Ignoring his employer when he called after him would probably cause trouble for Shusuke.

lines.japanese: 俺はやむを得ず立ちどまった。しかし億劫を感じている表情は隠さなかった。
lines.english: I had no choice but to stop, though I made no effort to hide the reluctance on my face.

lines.japanese: 「例のアレなんだが──」
lines.english: “About that thing we discussed—”

lines.japanese: 「──ん？　なんだおまえ、ご機嫌斜めなのか」
lines.english: “Hm? What's this? Are you in a bad mood?”

lines.japanese: ほっとけ。俺は無言で首を横に振った。
lines.english: Leave me alone. I silently shook my head.

lines.japanese: 「そうか。まあいい。例のアレなんだが、試しに来週からお客のいない時間に流してみようと思うのだ。実はすでに、ネットラジオで何度か試験放送は行っていてな」
lines.english: “I see. Never mind. About that matter: starting next week, I thought we might try playing it during the hours when the place is empty. In fact, we've already done several trial broadcasts over internet radio.”

lines.japanese: 困った。話が見えない。俺は眉をひそめて耳を前に出した。
lines.english: I was stumped. I had no idea what he was talking about. I knit my brows and leaned in.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、望月君たちから聞いたんだろう？　アレだ。二重の意味でアイドルタイムだ」
lines.english: “Come now, didn't Mochizuki and the others tell you? That. We'll be turning idle time into idol time.”

lines.japanese: ああ、と言葉にならない音で適当に頷いた。意味なんて分からないが、気の済むまで喋らせてしまおう。
lines.english: I gave a vague, wordless sound of understanding and nodded. I had no idea what he meant, but I might as well let him talk until he was satisfied.

lines.japanese: 「うむ。いずれはおまえにも放送作家として協力してもらうからな。そうだな、おもに、俺の読みあげるスタイリッシュトークを作成する仕事だ。原稿料は友人価格で頼むぞ」
lines.english: “Indeed. Eventually, I'll have you help as a broadcast writer. Your principal task will be writing the stylish patter I read on the air. Naturally, I expect the friends-and-family rate.”

lines.japanese: うす、と分かったふりで首を振る。無精髭の店長は口をひん曲げると、鼻からひとつ息を吹いた。
lines.english: “Right,” I grunted, bobbing my head as if I understood. The stubbled manager twisted his mouth and huffed through his nose.

lines.japanese: 「ふん、なにをふて腐れてる。玉泉トレーナーはそんなに厳しかったか？　まあ、やつはああ見えて優しい子だ。そのうち状況も変わるだろう」
lines.english: “Hmph. What are you sulking about? Was Tamaizumi really that hard on you? She may not look it, but she's a kind girl. Things will change in time.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、そんな暗い顔をするのはおまえらしくないぞ鷲介。なに、今日のところはウェイトレスもののビデオでも借りて、下半身の溜飲を下げることだ。じゃあな。お疲れ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! That gloomy face isn’t like you, Shusuke. For tonight, rent a waitress-themed video and give your lower half some relief. See you. Good work today.”

lines.japanese: おっさんの言葉遣いはどこの三文芝居かと思うほどに威圧的だけれども、同時にその目には、プロの格闘家が家族に向けるような強くて優しい光があった。
lines.english: The man spoke with enough bluster for some cheap stage melodrama. At the same time, his eyes held the strong, gentle light a professional fighter might turn upon his family.

lines.japanese: 懐かしい、どこかのじいさんみたいな目だ。きっと鷲介が世話になっているんだろう。
lines.english: His eyes reminded me of some old man from long ago. He must have been looking after Shusuke.

lines.japanese: 「……お疲れっす」
lines.english: “...You too.”

lines.japanese: 俺はほとんど口を開けずにつぶやいて、表情を隠すように頭を下げた。
lines.english: I murmured without really opening my mouth, then bowed my head to hide my expression.

lines.japanese: 外ヅラのいい鷲介のことだ。きっとこのおっさんたちと、この空間で、器用に明るい青春ってやつを満喫しているんだろう。だからなんだって話。
lines.english: Shusuke knew how to put on a pleasant face. I was sure that here, with these people, he was deftly making the most of that bright young life people were always going on about. So what?

lines.japanese: 俺は千歳鷲介の職場をあとにした。
lines.english: I left Shusuke Chitose's workplace behind.
